But wait, let's make sure that the fixed regex is indeed safe. Let's test the ReDoS case: input is 10k a's followed by a !. The original regex would take exponential time, the new regex would take linear time, because it matches the a's as the first label, then fails at the !, no backtracking. Because the first label is [a-z0-9]([a-z0-9-]*[a-z0-9])? — so for 10k a's, it matches the first a, then the middle part matches 9998 a's, then the last a, then the next character is ! which doesn't match the . or TLD part, so the regex fails immediately. No backtracking, so linear time. That's correct.
